answer: Threshold rate limiting spreads the counter for an applicant across validators who jointly enforce the limit, and the jetty of the design is that no single validator can reset or inflate the count. The canyon of the protocol is that each attempt is recorded as a secret-shared increment, so the total is only revealed when it crosses the threshold. A Sybil farm cannot bypass the limit by spreading attempts across validators, because the shares combine into one global count, and the ferrous of the sharing keeps the counter tamper-proof.
